Re:    Double E Pipeline, LLC
       Docket No. CP27-___-000
       Texas Mainline Compressor Station Project
       Abbreviated Application for a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity

Dear Ms. Reese:

Double E Pipeline, LLC (“Double E”) herewith files pursuant to and in accordance with Section
7(c) of the Natural Gas Act, 15 U.S.C. § 717f(c), and Part 157 of the Federal Energy Regulatory
Commission’s (“FERC” or “Commission”) regulations, 18 C.F.R. Part 157, an abbreviated
application for a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (“Application”) permitting
Double E to expand its interstate natural gas pipeline system through the requested activities
associated with the Texas Mainline Compressor Station Project (the “Project”). As discussed
below, the precedent agreements and market study submitted with the Application demonstrate a
demand for additional firm transportation service as soon as the Project can be completed and
placed into service. Double E is targeting an in-service date of October 1, 2028. In order to meet
this date, Double E requests that the Commission issue a certificate for the Project by October
2027, so that Double E may commence construction by November 2027.

Overview

The Project addresses a pressing energy infrastructure need: the growing demand for additional
firm natural gas transportation capacity to move surging Delaware Basin production to the Waha
Hub, the most liquid natural gas trading point in West Texas, at a time when existing pipeline
capacity connecting the two is insufficient. By adding a compressor station with two (2) natural
 Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
October 2, 2026
Page 2

gas-fired, turbine-driven centrifugal compressor units, totaling approximately 54,000 horsepower,
and associated facilities, on its existing interstate pipeline system in Loving County, Texas, Double
E will increase the system’s capability to transport natural gas from the northern Delaware Basin
in New Mexico to the Waha Hub in Texas by an additional approximately 800,000 dekatherms
per day (“Dth/d”). The Project will also give the system, for the first time, the physical capability
to reverse the direction of flow on its mainline, allowing Double E to transport gas northbound
physically, rather than solely by displacement, as market conditions and receipt and delivery
capabilities on the system develop. This significant capacity expansion will be achieved entirely
through new compression, and aside from piping connecting the system to the compression
facilities, will not require the construction of any new pipeline outside of the proposed compressor
station, maximizing the efficiency of Double E’s existing infrastructure while minimizing land
disturbance and environmental impact.

In addition to satisfying this pressing market need, the Project will bolster Double E’s ability to
safely, reliably, and efficiently transport natural gas, enhancing transportation reliability and
operational flexibility for existing and new shippers alike.

Market Need

The market need for the Project is clear and compelling. The Project is needed to increase the
currently limited natural gas transportation infrastructure in the northern Delaware Basin,
supporting long-term market demand for Delaware Basin natural gas.

U.S. natural gas demand is projected to grow heavily, driven by increasing liquefied natural gas
exports along the Gulf Coast, industrial consumption demand, and surging demand from power
generation, including rapidly expanding data centers, all of which require dependable access to
long-term natural gas supplies.

At the same time, the Delaware Basin, one of the fastest-growing natural gas producing regions in
the country, is generating increasing volumes of supply that are seeking access to downstream
markets. This growth in production is expected to continue, as the Energy Information
Administration (“EIA”) forecasts rising production of oil from the Delaware Basin, increasing the
associated production of natural gas in the area.

Existing options for natural gas takeaway from the area are currently both insufficient to
accommodate the growing production and directed primarily to the U.S. West Coast, where
demand is declining. The Project will provide needed relief. By unlocking access for additional
volumes to reach different downstream markets, the Project will enable consumers to put these
volumes to work for the economic and operational benefit of parties across the country, capturing
this clean-burning energy source for productive use and ensuring domestic energy security.
Conversely, without the Project, few beneficial options for the disposition of these volumes will
exist, as local demand is significantly below expected production levels and storage in the area is
also insufficient.
 Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
October 2, 2026
Page 3

The Waha Hub, situated at the terminus of Double E’s system, is the ideal destination for these
volumes: it is one of the most liquid natural gas trading points in the nation, with a rapidly
expanding portfolio of takeaway infrastructure expected to come online in the near future,
providing downstream market access to consumers and exporters across the country and abroad.
Yet the existing pipeline capacity connecting the Delaware Basin to the Waha Hub is insufficient.
By expanding Double E’s capacity to link surging Delaware Basin supply with Waha’s growing
takeaway capacity, the Project will strengthen a critical bridge between prolific natural gas
production and dynamic and growing markets, improving access to key end-use markets,
strengthening overall transportation reliability and market connectivity, and benefiting producers,
shippers, consumers, and the broader national economy.

Further illustrating the market need for the Project, Double E completed a successful open season
for the Project and executed binding precedent agreements for 400,000 Dth/d of Project capacity.
The Project is also appropriately sized: as discussed further in the Application, Double E selected
the proposed compressor station site based on numerous factors, including hydraulic assessments,
optimal compression characteristics, and the abilities to avoid impacts on cultural and
environmental resources and minimize noise-related impacts. Double E also continues to engage
in active commercial discussions with other prospective shippers who submitted indications of
interest in response to the open season and anticipates executing additional binding precedent
agreements for the remaining Project capacity in the near term. As the Commission and the D.C.
Circuit have repeatedly recognized, these binding, long-term shipper commitments constitute the
best evidence of market need for the Project. In addition, Double E is submitting a market study
with its Application which bolsters this evidence of need, demonstrating that the Project will help
provide a necessary bridge between substantial growth in northern Delaware Basin natural gas
supply and significant incremental demand at Waha.

Operational Benefits

In addition to delivering new capacity to satisfy market need and serve demonstrated shipper
demand, the Project will enhance the reliability and operational flexibility of Double E’s interstate
system in Texas and New Mexico, providing added benefits to new shippers and existing shippers
on the system alike, and to the broader market. These benefits align squarely with the national
energy policy objectives reflected in Executive Order No. 14156, Declaring a National Energy
Emergency, which calls for expedited approvals of energy transportation infrastructure as a matter
of national and economic security.

The Project is also needed to enhance the Double E pipeline system’s ability to safely, reliably,
and efficiently transport additional natural gas produced in the Delaware Basin to downstream
markets, and to enhance transportation reliability, market access, and operational flexibility.
Natural gas producers place significant value on reliable pipeline egress from processing
complexes, and the Double E pipeline has established a strong record of dependable service since
commencing operations. The additional compression installed by the Project would provide
existing and new shippers with increased transportation options, reduce constraints on movement
of natural gas out of the basin, and strengthen connections between natural gas suppliers and
growing demand centers. The Project will also improve system flexibility by increasing the ability
 Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
October 2, 2026
Page 4

of the system to accommodate changing receipt and delivery needs, thereby enhancing overall
operational responsiveness and efficiency, and giving the system the physical capability to reverse
the direction of flow on its mainline as market conditions develop.

Summary

In short, the Project is an efficient, cost-effective, and minimally invasive expansion of an existing
interstate pipeline system that will deliver immediate and durable public benefits, including
expanded access to critical natural gas supplies, enhanced market competition, increased
transportation capacity, and improved system reliability, at a time when such benefits are needed
most. The Project responds to surging Delaware Basin production and growing downstream
demand, is supported by binding shipper commitments and a market study demonstrating real
market need, and will provide meaningful operational flexibility for existing and new shippers
alike. The Commission should grant the requested authorizations without delay.

Double E also requests that information submitted in Volume IV and marked “CONTAINS
CRITICAL ENERGY INFRASTRUCTURE INFORMATION - DO NOT RELEASE” and

“CUI//CEII” be treated as Critical Energy Infrastructure Information pursuant to 18 C.F.R. §
388.113 of the Commission’s regulations. Double E is submitting Volume IV as CEII because it

UNITED STATES OF AMERICA

                   FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION



Double E Pipeline, LLC                             )                  Docket No. CP27-___-000


                      ABBREVIATED APPLICATION FOR
             CERTIFICATE OF PUBLIC CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY


       Pursuant to Section 7(c) of the Natural Gas Act (“NGA”), 15 U.S.C. § 717f(c), and Part

157 of the regulations of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or “Commission”),

18 C.F.R. Part 157, Double E Pipeline, LLC (“Double E”) hereby submits this abbreviated

application for a certificate of public convenience and necessity (“Application”) authorizing

Double E to undertake the requested activities associated with the Texas Mainline Compressor

Station Project in order to expand its interstate natural gas pipeline system (the “Project”).

       The Project responds to a growing need for firm pipeline capacity that connects expanding

natural gas output from the Delaware Basin, a producing area within the Permian Basin, to the

Waha Hub, a highly liquid trading point also within the Permian Basin with expanding takeaway

capability, at a time when the pipeline infrastructure linking the two is not keeping pace. The

Project will also strengthen the reliability and operational flexibility of the Double E system across

Texas and New Mexico and give the system, for the first time, the physical capability to reverse

the direction of flow on its mainline, for the benefit of all system shippers.

       The proposed Project will be entirely compression-based and will create an additional

approximately 800,000 dekatherms per day (“Dth/d”) of firm transportation capacity on Double

E’s existing pipeline system through the installation of a new compressor station consisting of two

(2) natural gas-fired, turbine-driven centrifugal compressor units, together rated at approximately
 54,000 horsepower, along with associated piping, valves, controls, coolers, conditioning facilities,

cathodic protection, and appurtenances in Loving County, Texas, as more specifically described

in Resource Report 1, submitted as part of the Environmental Report (“ER”) filed with this

Application as Exhibit F-I.

           Double E has executed binding precedent agreements which contemplate Double E’s

provision of long-term firm transportation service using Project capacity commencing as soon as

possible and is targeting an October 1, 2028 in-service date. Double E’s need for the Project is

further supported by a market study addressing demand for the Project’s capacity (“Market

Study”),1 which is being submitted with this Application.

           As discussed further herein, the Project satisfies the Commission’s Certificate Policy

Statement2 and is required by the public convenience and necessity. Double E requests that the

Commission issue a certificate order by October 2027, such that Double E may obtain

authorization to commence construction by November 2027, which should allow adequate time

for Double E to complete construction and place the Project into service by its October 1, 2028

target in-service date.

           In support of this Application, and consistent with the Commission’s regulations and Rules

of Practice and Procedure, Double E submits the following:

                                                I.
                                        EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

           The Project is intended to meet increasing demand for firm pipeline transportation capacity

that can carry natural gas out of the rapidly expanding Delaware Basin, one of the country’s fastest-

       B. Ensuring Compliance and Minimizing Community Impact.

           Double E has taken appropriate measures to minimize potential adverse impacts on

landowners and surrounding communities. Because the Project is entirely compression-based, its

practices. Double E has also evaluated the proximity of the Project Facilities to residential areas.

No noise sensitive areas are located within one mile of the Project facilities, and therefore no noise

                                       III.
                       DESCRIPTION OF EXISTING OPERATIONS

       Double E owns an interstate natural gas pipeline system, which is operated by a subsidiary

of Summit Midstream Corporation, which owns seventy percent (70%) of Double E. Subsidiaries

of Exxon Mobil Corporation own thirty percent (30%) of Double E, one of which is Double E’s

largest shipper. The pipeline system was originally placed into service in November 2021. The


                                                8
 system currently consists of approximately 140 miles of pipe with multiple receipt and delivery

meters (the “Pipeline”). The Pipeline runs from the northern portion of the Delaware Basin in

Eddy and Lea Counties, New Mexico down to the Waha Hub in West Texas, traversing Loving,

Ward, Reeves, and Pecos Counties in Texas. Currently, no compression facilities exist on the

Pipeline.

                                            IV.
                                    BACKGROUND AND NEED

           As discussed above, the Project will add firm natural gas transportation capacity within the

Permian Basin to accommodate the Delaware Basin’s expanding production and move it to the

Waha Hub, one of the nation’s most liquid natural gas trading points, at a time when nationwide

natural gas demand is projected to climb substantially over the coming years. The existing pipeline

infrastructure connecting the two currently falls short: the Market Study submitted with this

Application identifies an approximately 5.1 Bcf/d shortfall between projected Permian Basin

production growth and planned infrastructure connecting that production to Waha.11 The Project

will help close that gap by expanding the capacity of Double E’s existing system.

           To provide potential shippers with an opportunity to obtain Project capacity, Double E

conducted a binding open season from March 10 through August 31, 2026. As a result, Double E

executed binding precedent agreements contemplating Double E’s provision of long-term firm

transportation service on the Project for 400,000 Dth/d as soon as the Project is placed into service.

Double E also continues to work with prospective shippers who responded to the open season and

anticipates executing additional agreements in the near-term. Turnback capacity would not alter

the scope of the Project facilities since, rather than turning back capacity, almost all existing



11

 shippers are instead seeking additional capacity through the Project, and existing shippers not

doing so hold too little capacity to obviate the need for any proposed Project facilities.

            As the Commission has repeatedly held, and as the D.C. Circuit has confirmed, such

binding precedent agreements are the “best evidence” of market need for a proposed project,12

because they reflect the informed, negotiated commitments of the shippers who will actually pay

for and use the capacity and “involve sophisticated parties engaging in negotiations for pipeline

transportation services to meet individualized needs.”13 Under the general rule recognized by the

D.C. Circuit, the Commission “may find market need by relying solely on a precedent agreement,”

and there is only a narrow “exception to that rule” that allows the Commission to look beyond

precedent agreements—namely, “when an agreement involves affiliated entities and there is

‘plausible evidence of self-dealing.’”14 Stated plainly, “[a]bsent self-dealing, [the Commission is]

entitled to rely on the precedent agreement[s] without considering additional evidence.”15 No such

exception is triggered here, as there is no plausible evidence of self-dealing: Double E’s precedent

agreements reflect the informed, binding, long-term commitments of shippers who will actually

pay for the Project capacity, regardless of whether that capacity is ultimately used, and who are

best positioned to assess their own need for firm transportation.16

            Consistent with these principles, the D.C. Circuit has affirmed the Commission’s approval

of projects supported by binding precedent agreements without regard to the specific level of

 subscription.17 The Project’s subscription—binding precedent agreements executed by shippers

        The Project is also appropriately sized. The capacity the Project creates is a function of

the hydraulics of the existing Pipeline and the location of the proposed compressor station, which,

cost. The Project capacity not yet subscribed under binding precedent agreements reflects efficient

present the overbuilding concerns that the Certificate Policy Statement is designed to guard

against. Demand also continues to exist for the remaining Project capacity, as evidenced by Double

E’s ongoing commercial discussions with additional prospective Project shippers.

        This evidence of need is corroborated by the Market Study’s analysis of demand for the

Project’s capacity, which Double E is submitting with this Application. The Market Study projects

nearly 6.0 Bcf/d of additional northern Delaware Basin natural gas supply within proximity to the

Double E system by year-end 2030, and between 6.7 and 15.2 Bcf/d of incremental demand at

 Waha over the same period.18 The study further identifies a material infrastructure gap between

this growing northern Delaware Basin production and the long-haul transmission capacity

originating at Waha, concluding that additional intra-basin pipeline capacity is needed to connect

expanding gas plant supply with downstream markets.19 That need is reinforced by announced

processing expansions: the study identifies growing production from natural gas plants in the

Delaware Basin, many of them in Eddy and Lea Counties, New Mexico, and Loving County,

Texas, in proximity to the Pipeline.20 The Project is a significant step toward providing this needed

Public Convenience and Necessity for the Project. As discussed below, the Project satisfies the

Certificate Policy Statement and is required by the public convenience and necessity.

the Commission authorizing the construction, ownership, and operation of a new compressor

station consisting of two (2) natural gas-fired, turbine-driven centrifugal compressor units, together

rated at approximately 54,000 horsepower, along with associated piping, valves, controls, coolers,

conditioning facilities, cathodic protection, and appurtenances in Loving County, Texas, as more

specifically identified in Resource Report 1 submitted as part of the ER, and the additional capacity

that these facilities will create.

                                                    VI.
                                              RATE MATTERS

         Double E proposes to use its existing recourse rates under Rate Schedule FTS as the

applicable recourse rates for firm transportation service to be provided by the Project. As

demonstrated within Exhibit N, Double E’s existing approved recourse rates for transportation

under Rate Schedule FTS would be greater than the illustrative cost-based recourse rates for

transportation service on the Project calculated on a standalone basis. The Commission has

explained that “[w]here the currently-effective system recourse rate is greater than the estimated

incremental cost-based recourse rate, the Commission has found it appropriate to establish the

existing system rate as the initial recourse rate for the project.”21 Consistent with this policy,

Double E seeks approval to utilize its existing system Rate Schedule FTS recourse rates as the

initial recourse transportation rates for the Project.

         Double E also proposes to recover fuel costs associated with providing service on the

Project facilities through its existing Transporter’s Use percentage set forth in Section 22.1 of the

General Terms and Conditions of Double E’s Tariff. Use of this existing mechanism is appropriate

because, although Double E does not currently use fuel to provide transportation services, the

Transporter’s Use percentage in Section 22.1 was expressly designed to recover fuel usage and

any lost and unaccounted-for gas.22 Recovering fuel through the Transporter’s Use percentage

assessed to all shippers is also appropriate given the significant systemwide operational benefits

of the compression. The Project’s compression facilities are designed to compress the full

Charges and Surcharges.”)

 throughput of Double E’s mainline in both the forwardhaul (north to south) and backhaul (south

to north) directions, giving Double E the physical capability to reverse the direction of flow on its

mainline, in addition to its existing capability to provide backhauls by displacement. In both

directions, the compression will provide pressure support for the entire system, increasing the

reliability of meeting delivery point requirements and increasing the quantity of gas supply that

can enter the system from receipt points. The station’s fuel consumption is therefore a cost of

operating the integrated system for the benefit of all shippers, and all shippers should accordingly

share responsibility for the fuel associated with the service they receive.

           All of the binding precedent agreements with the Project shippers contemplate that service

will be provided at negotiated rates, in accordance with the Commission’s Negotiated Rate Policy

Statement23 and Double E’s Tariff. Double E will file all executed negotiated rate service

agreements with the Commission pursuant to the Commission’s rules and regulations.

                                           VII.
                             PUBLIC CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY

           The Project is required by the public convenience and necessity. The Certificate Policy

Statement establishes criteria for determining whether there is a need for a proposed project and

whether the proposed project will serve the public interest.24 It explains that, in deciding whether

to authorize the construction of new facilities, the Commission balances the public benefits of such

construction against the potential adverse consequences, if any.25




23
  Nat. Gas Pipelines Negotiated Rate Policies and Practices, 104 FERC ¶ 61,134 (2003), order on reh’g, 114 FERC
¶ 61,042 (2006).
24
     Gulf South Pipeline Company, LLC, 195 FERC ¶ 61,042, at P 9 (2026).
25
     Id.



                                                        14
             The threshold requirement for a project applicant is that it be prepared to financially

support the project without relying on subsidization from its existing customers.26                  The

Commission then determines whether the applicant has made efforts to eliminate or minimize any

adverse effects the project might have on the applicant’s existing customers, existing pipelines in

the market and their captive customers, and landowners and communities affected by the new

facilities.27 If the residual adverse effects on these interest groups are identified after efforts have

been made to minimize them, the Commission will then evaluate the project by balancing the

evidence of public benefits to be achieved against the residual adverse effects.28 This is essentially

an economic test.29 When the benefits outweigh the adverse effects on economic interests, the

Commission proceeds to complete the environmental analysis, where other interests are

considered.30

            For the reasons explained herein, the proposed Project satisfies all of the Certificate Policy

Statement’s requirements.

       A. Existing Customers Will Not Subsidize the Project.

            As discussed above, the threshold requirement for pipelines proposing new projects is that

the applicant must be prepared to financially support the project without relying on subsidization

from its existing customers. As discussed in Article VI above, Exhibit N demonstrates that the

illustrative cost-based recourse rates for transportation service on the Project would be lower than

Double E’s existing approved recourse rates for transportation under Rate Schedule FTS, and

 Double E intends to apply its existing system Rate Schedule FTS recourse rates as the initial

recourse transportation rates for the Project. The Commission has previously held that, in such

circumstances, a project is not subsidized by existing customers.31 With respect to fuel, Double E

submits that existing customers will not be inequitably burdened by including the Project’s fuel

costs into Double E’s Transporter’s Use percentage because they will receive substantial, concrete

operational benefits from the proposed facilities—namely, as discussed in Article VI, the physical

capability, for the first time, to reverse the direction of flow on Double E’s mainline, which will

position all shippers to transport gas northbound physically, rather than through displacement, as

market conditions and receipt and delivery capabilities on the system develop. Because these

benefits flow directly from the compression facilities responsible for the fuel increase, Double E

submits that sharing the associated fuel costs system-wide is just and reasonable.

       B. The Project Will Have No Adverse Impacts on Existing Customers or Existing
          Pipelines in the Market or Their Captive Customers.

           The proposed Project will not adversely impact service to Double E’s existing customers

or existing pipelines in the market or their captive customers. First, with respect to Double E’s

existing customers, the flow diagrams and information submitted as Exhibits G, G-I, and G-II

hereto demonstrate that the proposed compression facilities will not degrade their service. Nor

will existing shippers subsidize the Project, as established above. Further, Double E is not

proposing in this proceeding any changes to its Tariff that would in any way restrict existing

customers’ rights. In fact, rather than adversely impacting Double E’s existing customers, the

proposed Project will bolster the reliability and operational flexibility of Double E’s system, give

 the system the physical capability to reverse the direction of flow on its mainline, and improve

existing customers’ access to growing production in the Delaware Basin.

           Similarly, the proposed Project will not adversely impact existing pipelines in the market

or their captive customers. The Project is not being proposed to replace existing service received

on any other pipeline or displace existing service providers.32 To the contrary, the Project is in the

public interest because it will serve the Project shippers’ needs for additional firm transportation

capacity while enhancing the reliability and operational flexibility of Double E’s system for all of

its shippers.

           Accordingly, the Commission should conclude that, consistent with the Certificate Policy

Statement, the Project will have no adverse effects on Double E’s existing customers or existing

pipelines in the market or their captive customers.

       C. Double E Has Minimized Potential Adverse Impacts to Landowners and
          Communities.

           There will be minimal to no adverse impacts to landowners or the surrounding communities

associated with the proposed Project. As discussed in Article VIII, Double E will apply best

practices for environmental protection, noise reduction, and construction management, as

applicable. In addition, Article IX describes in detail Double E’s proactive engagement with local

officials and community members, and its commitment to continuing collaborative, respectful, and

productive discussions with them. Article X explains Double E’s outreach to and ongoing

cooperative discussions with affected landowners. As shown in the Resource Reports submitted

with the ER, the chosen site offers landowners and the surrounding community meaningful

benefits: it was selected in part based on its low anticipated environmental impacts, and it lies in



32
     Certificate Policy Statement at 61,748.



                                                  17
 an area already with low population density characterized by extensive oil and gas infrastructure,

with no nearby residences and no designated scenic or recreational areas, such that the Project’s

visual and community impacts are expected to be minimal. The Commission should conclude that

Double E has taken significant steps to minimize impacts to landowners and communities.

       D. Project Benefits Outweigh Any Potential Residual Adverse Impacts.

           As discussed above, the proposed Project is not anticipated to result in any residual adverse

impacts to Double E’s existing customers, existing pipelines in the market or their captive

customers, or landowners and communities affected by the new facilities. However, to the extent

that any such impacts arise, the Project’s benefits substantially outweigh them.

           First, the Project is needed, as evidenced by the long-term binding precedent agreements

executed by Project shippers and the Market Study submitted with this Application. The binding

precedent agreements alone provide sufficient evidence of market need: the Commission “may

find market need by relying solely on a precedent agreement” absent plausible evidence of self-

dealing, and no such evidence exists here.33 The Market Study bolsters this evidence of need,

demonstrating that the Project will help provide a necessary bridge between substantial growth in

northern Delaware Basin natural gas supply and significant incremental demand at Waha.

           In addition, the proposed Project will create numerous operational and economic benefits

for Double E’s existing system and all of its shippers, the natural gas market, and the country at

large.34 It will help close a demonstrated gap in the pipeline infrastructure connecting rapidly

growing Delaware Basin production to the Waha Hub, thereby enhancing the country’s access to

                                                       18
 natural gas supplies and increasing competition in the natural gas market at a time when demand

for natural gas will continue to grow. At the same time, it will bolster the reliability and operational

flexibility of Double E’s system and give the system the physical capability to reverse the direction

of flow on its mainline, ensuring these benefits continue to accrue into the future. These benefits

greatly outweigh any potential residual adverse impacts that may arise from the Project, consistent

with the Certificate Policy Statement.

    E. The Project is Required by the Public Convenience and Necessity.

In sum, (i) no existing Double E shippers will subsidize the Project, (ii) Double E has taken steps

to minimize or eliminate all adverse impacts on Double E’s existing customers, existing pipelines

in the market and their captive customers, and landowners and communities affected by the new

facilities, and (iii) if any such adverse impacts were to arise, the Project benefits will substantially

outweigh them. The Commission should therefore conclude that the Project is required by the

public convenience and necessity.

                                         VIII.
                                ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS

    A. Environmental Impacts.

        Double E is committed to protecting the natural environment and minimizing impacts on

the ecosystems and habitats in the areas where it operates. As detailed in the ER, Double E

carefully evaluated potential sites to reduce or avoid impacts to wetlands and waterbodies, listed

species, sensitive habitats, migratory birds, cultural resources, visual impacts, air and noise

impacts, natural, recreational, or wild and scenic areas, and other environmental resources.

        The proposed construction will incorporate proven construction techniques and mitigation

procedures and will result in no significant impact to the quality of human health, the environment,

or affected landowners. Utilizing construction and restoration methods that comply with the



                                                  19
 Commission’s 2013 Upland Erosion Control Revegetation and Maintenance Plan and Wetland and

Waterbody Construction and Mitigation Procedures will ensure that any adverse impacts are

limited and temporary.

       Copies of the applicable agency consultation letters necessary under the Endangered

Species Act, the National Historic Preservation Act, the Clean Air Act, and the Clean Water Act

are included in the attached ER. Double E has engaged in consultations and coordination with the

affected federal, state, and local government agencies, and appropriate federally-recognized tribes,

concerning the proposed construction activities associated with the Project, and will continue to

discuss specific concerns or requirements should they be raised.

       Construction of the proposed Project will require the use of a total of approximately 17.90

acres of land, resulting in both temporary and permanent land disturbance. Following construction

activities, operation of the Project will require approximately 15.80 acres of land, and the areas

necessary to facilitate construction, access roads, and temporary workspaces will be restored to

pre-construction conditions.

   B. Noise.

       Because the proposed compressor station is a new, greenfield facility, a sound level survey

of existing conditions is not applicable, consistent with the Commission’s filing requirements for

new compressor station sites. Double E has evaluated the anticipated noise profile of the selected

compressor units and ancillary equipment based on manufacturer specifications. As reflected in

Appendix 9-D to the ER, there are no noise sensitive areas within one mile of the proposed

compressor station, though there are several oil and gas operations within the area with sound

levels near 80 dB. Based on the modeling analysis, during operations Double E expects sound

levels in the area to remain mostly unchanged. The proposed compressor station is designed to




                                                20
 meet FERC’s requirements and ensure compliance with all relevant noise regulations. Further

detail regarding the Project’s noise analysis is provided in Resource Report 9, submitted with the

ER.

   C. Air Emissions.

       Double E has conducted required analyses to determine the potential impacts the Project

would have on air quality in the Project area. To minimize and mitigate the impacts identified in

those analyses, Double E will implement equipment, controls, and operating practices that meet or

exceed applicable regulatory requirements. Measures proposed to minimize air quality impacts

include the use of clean-burning natural gas as the fuel for all stationary combustion devices, and

good operating practices. All measures will be implemented in accordance with all applicable

federal, state, and local regulations, as detailed in Resource Report 9, submitted with the ER.

       Potential emissions from the proposed units and new ancillary sources associated with the

Project are below the Prevention of Significant Deterioration (“PSD”) major source threshold of

250 tons per year for each criteria pollutant, so the Project will not require PSD permitting. The

proposed units will be subject to applicable federal standards and regulations governing stationary

combustion turbines, including applicable New Source Performance Standards, and Double E will

ensure that all monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting requirements from those regulations are

met in accordance with the specified timeframes.

       Double E has applied or will apply for all necessary federal, state, and local air permits

required for construction and operation of the Project facilities. Resource Report 1, submitted with

the ER, describes all such permits.

        D. Alternatives.

           Under the no-action alternative, Double E would not construct the proposed Project. If the

proposed facilities were not constructed, the adverse impacts identified in the Project resource

reports would be avoided; however, the substantial beneficial impacts of implementing the Project

would also not occur, including the addition of approximately 800,000 Dth/d of firm transportation

capacity to meet the demands of the Project shippers and to help address the existing shortfall in

pipeline connectivity between the Delaware Basin and the Waha Hub and its expanding

downstream markets, as well as the enhanced reliability, operational flexibility, and capability to

reverse the direction of flow that the Project will provide to all shippers on Double E’s system.

The no-action alternative would fail to serve the demonstrated market need for additional capacity

on Double E’s system and would deprive the country of substantial public benefits at a time of

growing natural gas demand.

           Double E evaluated whether the Project’s capacity expansion could be accomplished

through system alternatives, including a review of existing pipeline capacity serving the Delaware

Basin and the Waha Hub. That review confirmed that rising New Mexico Delaware Basin

production has outpaced the state’s traditional westbound markets, which have seen declining

consumption, while the Waha Hub already has substantial existing takeaway capacity, with

additional capacity currently under construction, underscoring the need for additional firm

transportation capacity linking Delaware Basin supply to Waha rather than for new downstream

outlets.35 After thorough review, Double E determined that the proposed compression-based

expansion of its own system is the most efficient, cost-effective, and environmentally sound

approach to providing the additional capacity and system-wide operational benefits the Project


35

 will create. The addition of new pipeline laterals or looping of the existing pipeline segments was

not evaluated as a reasonable alternative because the existing Double E system has sufficient

capacity to accommodate the proposed incremental volumes. As a result, the evaluation of system

alternatives was limited to the addition of compression facilities and the identification of suitable

locations for such facilities, as these represented the only practicable means of increasing system

throughput within the existing pipeline network. The compression-only approach avoids the need

for substantial new pipeline right-of-way acquisition, minimizes land disturbance, and leverages

Double E’s existing infrastructure, resulting in a smaller footprint and reduced environmental

impact as compared to alternative approaches.

       Double E also evaluated multiple potential alternative compressor station sites along its

pipeline system, including a site at the Poker Lake receipt point, a site near the middle of the

pipeline route, and a site near the end of the pipeline route, in addition to the proposed site. As

discussed further in Resource Report 10, the location and units proposed herein present the best

solution for the Project based on numerous factors, including hydraulic assessments, optimal

compression characteristics, and the abilities to avoid impacts on cultural and environmental

resources and minimize noise-related impacts.

       The Commission should conclude that the proposed Project represents the superior

alternative for meeting the demonstrated need for additional firm transportation capacity on

Double E’s system.

operate, and maintain a new compressor station, comprised of two (2) compressor units and
associated piping, valves, controls, coolers, conditioning facilities, cathodic protection, and
appurtenances, in Loving County, Texas, in order to create an additional approximately 800,000
dekatherms per day of capacity on its interstate pipeline system to bring growing production in the
Delaware Basin to the liquid Waha Hub and increase the reliability and operational flexibility of
the system.

        Any questions regarding the proposed project should be directed to Jerry Castillo, Director
of Regulatory Affairs, Summit Midstream Corporation, 910 Louisiana Street, Suite 4200, Houston,
TX 77002, phone: (832) 930-6524, email: jerry.castillo@summitmidstream.com. Any person
desiring to intervene or to protest this filing must file in accordance with Rules 211 and 214 of the
Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure (18 C.F.R. 385.211 and 385.214). Protests will be
considered by the Commission in determining the appropriate action to be taken, but will not serve
to make protestants parties to the proceeding. Any person wishing to become a party must file a
notice of intervention or motion to intervene, as appropriate. Such notices, motions, or protests
must be filed on or before the comment date. Anyone filing a motion to intervene or protest must
serve a copy of that document on the applicant. On or before the comment date, it is not necessary
to serve motions to intervene or protests on persons other than the applicant.

       The Commission encourages electronic submission of protests and interventions in lieu of
paper using the “eFiling” link at http://www.ferc.gov. Persons unable to file electronically should
submit an original and 3 copies of the protest or intervention to the Federal Energy Regulatory
Commission, Attn: Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary, 888 First Street, NE, Washington, DC
20426.
